title: What the Motors and the Battery Allow: Top Speed, Acceleration and Climb From a Drive Train, and Which of the Motors or the Grip Is the One That Runs Out First

questions.question: What gives a brushed motor its force at the wheel?
options: The torque-speed line, through the gearbox, over the wheel radius
questions.explanation: Stall torque at rest, none at the no load speed.

questions.question: A battery of 0.5 ohm cut the standing acceleration from 4.54 to:
questions.explanation: The bus sags under the standing current.

questions.question: The top speed on level gravel was:
options: 1.67 m/s, under the no load speed
questions.explanation: The rolling resistance takes the rest.

questions.question: On gravel the limit on the acceleration was the:
questions.explanation: Grip runs out before the motors.

questions.question: Why is it money wasted to buy stronger motors for a grip limited robot?
options: The tyres cannot hold the extra force, so the acceleration does not change

questions.question: Why was the vehicle tuned on a fresh battery wrong on a tired one?
options: A tired battery sags more under the standing current
